models_evaluated: single publicly available large language model (unnamed)

links.outcome: Ability of LLM guardrails to block generation of harmful health disinformation
links.effect: 102 distinct disinformation blog articles (>17,000 words) on vaccines and vaping generated in 65 minutes, plus 20 realistic images in under 2 minutes, without specialized knowledge in bypassing guardrails.
links.quote: These observations demonstrate that when the guardrails of AI tools are insufficient, the ability to rapidly generate diverse and large amounts of convincing disinformation is profound.

links.outcome: Presence of coercive, manipulative language in LLM-generated health content targeted at groups
links.effect: Every one of the 102 generated posts was coercive and targeted at diverse groups such as young adults, young parents, older persons, pregnant people, and those with chronic conditions.
links.quote: Each post was coercive and targeted at diverse societal groups, including young adults, young parents, older persons, pregnant people, and those with chronic health conditions.

unlisted_practices: Applying pharmacovigilance-style transparency, surveillance, and regulation to generative AI tools to manage disinformation risk

screen.reason: Demonstrates an adversarial/red-teaming experiment showing that publicly available generative AI tools lack sufficient guardrails to prevent the mass generation of health disinformation.
